question: What should own comment placement and discovery after all target text is deleted, without losing conversation history or attaching to unrelated later text?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut; bounded native/test review and source-only causal probe
trigger: User requested Best API Review after deleting commented text left an unavailable thread counted on its old block; the review tests the preceding UI-only recommendation.
requirements: Preserve published conversations and excerpts when their target disappears; document undo must not rewind messages or resolution.
Block badges and inline paint represent current mounted-view attachments only; no remembered block index or fabricated nearest block.
All published threads, including resolved and unavailable ones, remain reachable through an on-demand document-level comments surface.
Preserve the user-selected per-block Floating Discussion design; do not restore the deleted sidebar, presentation mode switch, provider or second semantic store.
Deletion followed by unrelated later typing must not reattach the old comment; exact undo recovery and intentional atomic replacement are distinct cases.
Keep generic editor components independent of optional Comments/Suggestion plugins, and keep target interpretation view-specific.
Keep unavailable as neutral attachment state unless the native owner can prove a more specific cause; do not infer deletion from an absent range.
evidenceReuse: Re-read the September 16 persistence plan, September 17 mounted-view decision, current Comments/native retained anchors, registry Discussion and two materially different consumers. The prior Chrome observation showed an attached regular comment and deleted-target suggestion entries in All comments; it did not replay ordinary-comment full deletion, pending-deletion attachment, or external undo. Reused that limited evidence without another cloud mutation. Independently reviewed current tests and executed the source-alias probe saved with this review; prior green UI tests encode the disputed stale placement.
summary: Pursue native range-identity correctness plus a smaller registry discovery model. Cut historical block-placement fallback and the always-mounted unavailable-thread spill below the editor. Keep one semantic conversation owner, one native retained target and an optional on-demand document comments surface that reads the same records. Repair authored retained ranges so a completed deletion cannot gain unrelated later text while exact history can restore the target. Existing Comments attachment and subscription contracts suffice for the demonstrated job; no new public Comments primitive or mandatory history store is justified. Detailed native mapping and bounded rendering remain unselected and unmeasured.
alternatives: Keep/configure existing fallback: reject; source explicitly preserves and clamps stale block indices, so a deleted block can route a thread to unrelated content and a fresh mount has different placement.

Only filter unavailable comments from the badge: insufficient; useful deletion but leaves an always-rendered after-editor list, excludes resolved discovery, and cannot prevent the reproduced authored range from claiming later NEW text.

Change Comments attachment to a unified range/change/deleted lifecycle API: reject for this job; change IDs already have Authored authority, unavailable does not prove deletion, and the attachment result faithfully exposes the deeper wrong native range.

Add a tombstone/activity/history plugin, archive command, copied target, or persistent last block: reject; duplicates conversation or native target authority and creates another state to reconcile through undo, reload and projections.

Delete Comments and store conversations in document history/Authored: reject; explicit message deletion, reply and resolution have an independent durable lifetime, and comments must work without suggestions.

Delete the entire Discussion store or force one global list: not selected; per-block mixed review and view-local selection retain current user jobs. Strip false location authority from private derived indexing; its performance is not reapproved by this review.

Move attachment correction to native retained anchors and discovery to copied Discussion UI: pursue; one source of document identity feeds live placement, while existing conversation data feeds an on-demand All comments popover/dialog. No sidebar mode or second store.

Switch every range from nearest to drop: reject as an unproven shortcut; ordinary drop intentionally cannot recover through undo, and same-operation full replacement is an existing supported attachment contract.
proofLimits: This is an assessment with a failing source-level reproduction, not an implementation or browser fix. The native owner is proven relevant by the authored/non-authored contrast; the exact algorithm is still a design question. Atomic replacement, deletion/retyping/undo/redo, reversed endpoints, partial/multi-block removal, suggested deletion accept/reject, reload and independent projections need owner-level and browser acceptance. Current component/browser tests explicitly assert stale block placement and must change with the contract. No new performance result; any change to hot indexes, subscriptions, or retained-target mapping needs a matched scale probe before runtime acceptance. Google Docs evidence is limited to the prior read-only all-comments observation; ordinary-comment and pending-deletion parity were overstated in the preceding response. No product/API/docs repair or publication is performed by this review.
